summary: The Multilateral Alignment of Technology Controls on Hardware (MATCH) Act directs federal agencies to prioritize diplomatic efforts with allied supplier countries to align export controls on semiconductor manufacturing equipment. It requires reviews of semiconductor equipment and facilities, mandates the implementation of United States export restrictions and licensing requirements if diplomatic efforts fail or are exhausted, and requires regular reporting to Congress.

affected_groups.effect: Subject to new and continued export restrictions, licensing requirements with a policy of denial, and prohibitions on servicing equipment at covered facilities in countries of concern.
Required to conduct reviews, engage in continuous diplomatic outreach, issue regulations, make formal certifications to Congress, and submit regular reports.
affected_groups.group: Federal agencies (Department of Commerce and Department of State)

affected_groups.effect: Subject to ongoing diplomatic engagement by United States officials encouraging the adoption of aligned export controls and license restrictions on semiconductor manufacturing equipment.

key_provisions: Requires the Secretary of Commerce and the Secretary of State to jointly conduct a review within 60 days to identify covered semiconductor manufacturing equipment and facilities, and to submit lists to Congress and the Federal Register.

Mandates that federal agency heads immediately engage in diplomatic efforts with allied supplier countries to adopt countrywide controls and license requirements with a policy of denial for covered facilities.

Requires the Secretary of Commerce, in consultation with the Secretary of State, to issue regulations within 150 days applying countrywide controls to U.S.-produced semiconductor manufacturing equipment and end-user or end-use restrictions to covered facilities in countries of concern.

Allows for a one-time national security waiver of up to 90 days to extend the certification deadline under specific conditions involving consultations with the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Energy.

Provides for the termination or modification of controls on items exported from allied supplier countries if those countries establish equivalent controls, and for the reimposition of controls if allied countries weaken or revoke their policies.

Requires ongoing annual and specific periodic reports and briefings to appropriate congressional committees concerning the status of semiconductor controls, diplomatic efforts, and lists of restricted equipment and entities.
missing_information: Specific details on the exact positive incentives that will be utilized during diplomatic engagements.
The precise economic cost or trade volume affected by the newly mandated export restrictions and licensing requirements.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Multilateral Alignment of Technology Controls on Hardware (MATCH) Act directs federal agencies to prioritize diplomatic efforts with allied supplier countries to align export controls on semiconductor manufacturing equipment. It requires reviews of semiconductor equipment and facilities, mandates the implementation of United States export restrictions and licensing requirements if diplomatic efforts fail or are exhausted, and requires regular reporting to Congress.
summary_detail.significance: This legislation addresses national security and international technology trade by mandating a coordinated framework of export restrictions, licensing policies, and diplomatic engagement regarding semiconductor manufacturing equipment. Its potential impact depends on the degree of diplomatic alignment achieved with allied nations and the implementation of regulatory controls on specified technologies and entities.
